description: Given the root of a binary search tree, return a balanced binary search tree with the same node values. A balanced BST is one where the depth of the two subtrees of every node never differs by more than 1.
intuition: In-order traversal of a BST gives sorted values. Building a balanced BST from a sorted array is easy: pick the middle element as root and recurse on each half. It is like creating a balanced tournament bracket.
approach: Perform an in-order traversal to get sorted values. Then recursively build a balanced BST from the sorted array by always choosing the middle element as root.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: root = [1,null,2,null,3,null,4] (right-skewed tree)

In-order traversal: vals = [1, 2, 3, 4]

build(0, 3):
  mid=1, root=vals[1]=2
  left = build(0, 0):
    mid=0, root=vals[0]=1, left=null, right=null -> node(1)
  right = build(2, 3):
    mid=2, root=vals[2]=3
    left = build(2,1) -> null
    right = build(3,3):
      mid=3, root=vals[3]=4 -> node(4)
    -> node(3, null, 4)
  -> node(2, node(1), node(3,null,4))

Result: [2,1,3,null,null,null,4] (balanced)
explanation:
1. In-order traversal of a BST gives sorted values.
2. Build a balanced BST from the sorted array.
3. Choose the middle element as root to ensure balance.
4. Recursively build left subtree from left half and right subtree from right half.
5. This produces a height-balanced BST.
hints: In-order traversal of a BST gives sorted values.
From a sorted array, always picking the middle element as root gives a balanced tree.
Recursively apply this to left and right halves.
